rv.q: Bill Alexander’s production is certainly enjoyable in its camp and bitchy way, but finally fails to deliver the knockout dramatic blows that made the movie so memorable.
Because they have so much fun with the roles, we have fun, too, even if Anton Burge's script never digs far beneath the surface...
In the end, the show’s far too nice for its own good.

cn.t: Mixed reviews for this backstage drama about Davis and Crawford's legendary rivalry, with critics finding some humor but ultimately deeming it overlong and lacking the camp fireworks the subject matter deserves.
